title: Near-Field Characterisation of Guided Modes in WS2 Nanobeams and Quasi-Bulk Crystals
authors: Zara S. Taylor, Luke M. Hallacy, Xuerong Hu, Oliver T. Williams, Simone Strohmair, Fabian Felixberger, Alexander J. Knight, Timothy Chester-Parsons, Luke R. Wilson, Alexander I. Tartakovskii
abstract: The exceptionally high in-plane refractive index, low sub-bandgap absorption, and strong optical anisotropy of WS2 make it a promising material platform for next-generation integrated circuits for nanophotonics. Its layered van der Waals structure further enables heterogeneous integration with silicon photonics and emerging two-dimensional optoelectronic materials. However, despite increasing interest in the waveguiding properties of WS2, experimental studies of wavelength-dependent modal confinement and attenuation remain limited. Additionally, though the extinction coefficient of WS2 is expected to be near-negligible beneath the bandgap, reported values span orders of magnitude, leading to large uncertainty in predicted modal decay lengths and wafer-scale integration feasibility. To resolve these ambiguities we perform hyperspectral cavity-enhanced imaging, determining high-resolution upper and lower bounds on the extinction coefficient of WS2 within the visible-NIR edge. We further employ scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) to probe TE0, TM0, and higher-order modes in both quasi-bulk and nanobeam WS2 waveguides across the 800-1400 nm spectral range, enabling identification of mode-specific trends in wavevector dispersion and loss. This work simultaneously assesses s-SNOM as a probe of waveguide performance, and we find that while absolute loss values depend on measurement geometry, s-SNOM reliably captures relative modal trends and provides upper bounds on propagation loss, supporting its use as a diagnostic tool for anisotropic waveguides. We further identify significant artefacts in nanobeam measurements arising from transverse interference and spatial sampling effects when the structure size approaches the excitation wavelength, which can shift extracted effective indices by up to 0.25.
summary: This work characterizes guided optical modes ($	ext{TE}_0$ and $	ext{TM}_0$) in WS2 nanobeams and bulk crystals using advanced near-field techniques like s-SNOM. By mapping modal dispersion and measuring material absorption, the authors establish robust diagnostic protocols for assessing waveguiding quality in these promising 2D materials.
main_problem: The study addresses the limited experimental understanding of wavelength-dependent modal confinement and attenuation in WS2 waveguides, complicated by ambiguities in reported material extinction coefficients.
main_result: s-SNOM reliably captures relative modal trends for TE0 and TM0 modes across 800–1400 nm, confirming its utility as a diagnostic tool despite absolute loss values depending on measurement geometry.
method: The authors employed hyperspectral cavity-enhanced imaging (iCEAS) to bound the extinction coefficient and utilized scattering-type s-SNOM microscopy to probe guided modes in both quasi-bulk and nanobeam WS2 waveguides.
model_or_system: The physical system is WS2, a layered van der Waals material promising for nanophotonics due to its high refractive index and optical anisotropy. Measurements are performed on patterned nanobeams and larger quasi-bulk crystals deposited on an SiO2/Si substrate.
key_observables: Effective refractive indices (neff), modal confinement, propagation loss ($	ext{dB}/	ext{mm}$), and the extinction coefficient ($\kappa$) as functions of wavelength and geometry.
important_parameters: Wavelength range: 800–1400 nm; key modes: $	ext{TE}_0$ and $	ext{TM}_0$; critical thickness regimes (e.g., $112 \pm 5 	ext{ nm}$).
main_assumptions: Absolute loss values measured by s-SNOM depend on measurement geometry, and nanobeam measurements can suffer from artifacts due to transverse interference or spatial sampling effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate iCEAS extinction maps, simulated/measured mode dispersion curves ($	ext{neff}$ vs. $\lambda$), field profiles showing TE0/TM0 confinement factors, and Fourier Transform peak fitting results for different modes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically moves from characterizing the material absorption (iCEAS) to mapping modal behavior in quasi-bulk crystals using s-SNOM, and finally analyzing mode dispersion and artifacts in highly confined nanobeams across a wide spectral range.
why_interesting: While focused on photonics, the detailed analysis of wave propagation in anisotropic 2D materials provides insights into boundary conditions and field confinement that are relevant for designing quantum optical cavities or waveguides interacting with quantum emitters.
